<HR  SIZE="3" style="COLOR:#999999" WIDTH="100%" ALIGN="CENTER">

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Background Information </B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">On June&nbsp;7, 2013, Liberty Global, Inc., a Delaware corporation (&#147;<U>Liberty Global</U>&#148;), Liberty Global plc, a public
limited company organized under English law (formerly known as Lynx Europe Limited) (the &#147;<U>Company</U>&#148;) and Virgin Media Inc., a Delaware corporation (&#147;<U>Virgin Media</U>&#148;) completed the previously-announced business
combination transaction pursuant to which the Company became the publicly-held parent company of the successors by merger to Liberty Global and Virgin Media (the &#147;<U>Mergers</U>&#148;). In connection with the Mergers and pursuant to the
Agreement and Plan of Merger dated as of February&nbsp;5, 2013, as amended on March&nbsp;6, 2013 (the &#147;<U>Merger Agreement</U>&#148;), by and among Liberty Global, the Company, Lynx US MergerCo 1 LLC (&#147;<U>Lynx Merger Sub 1</U>&#148;), Lynx
US MergerCo 2 LLC (&#147;<U>Lynx Merger Sub 2</U>&#148;), Viper US MergerCo 1 LLC (&#147;<U>Viper Merger Sub 1</U>&#148;), Viper US MergerCo 2 LLC (&#147;<U>Viper Merger Sub 2</U>&#148;) and Virgin Media, (a)&nbsp;Viper Merger Sub 2 was merged with
and into Virgin Media, with Virgin Media as the surviving entity (the &#147;<U>First Viper Merger</U>&#148;), (b)&nbsp;immediately thereafter, and as part of the same plan, Virgin Media as the surviving entity was then merged with and into Viper
Merger Sub 1, with Viper Merger Sub 1 as the surviving entity (renamed Virgin Media Inc.), (c)&nbsp;immediately thereafter, and as part of the same plan, Lynx Merger Sub 2 was merged with and into Liberty Global, with Liberty Global as the surviving
entity (the &#147;<U>First Lynx Merger</U>&#148;), and (d)&nbsp;immediately thereafter, and as part of the same plan, Liberty Global as the surviving entity was then merged with and into Lynx Merger Sub 1, with Lynx Merger Sub 1 as the surviving
entity (renamed Liberty Global, Inc.). </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In connection with the First Viper Merger, each share of common stock, par value $0.01
per share, of Virgin Media was converted into the right to receive (a)&nbsp;0.2582 of a Class&nbsp;A ordinary share of the Company, (b)&nbsp;0.1928 of a Class C ordinary share of the Company and (c)&nbsp;$17.50 in cash (without interest). In
connection with the First Lynx Merger, each share of Series A common stock, par value $0.01 per share, of Liberty Global was converted into the right to receive one Class&nbsp;A ordinary share of the Company, each share of Series B common stock, par
value $0.01 per share, of Liberty Global was converted into the right to receive one Class B ordinary share of the Company and each share of Series C common stock, par value $0.01 per share, of Liberty Global was converted into the right to receive
one Class C ordinary share of the Company. Each Class&nbsp;A ordinary share of the Company will be entitled to one vote per share, each Class B ordinary share of the Company will be entitled to ten votes per share and each Class C ordinary shares of
the Company will be issued without voting rights. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Based on the number of shares of common stock of Liberty Global and Virgin
Media that were outstanding as of June 6, 2013, the Company had outstanding, immediately following the closing of the Mergers, approximately 211.6 million Class A ordinary shares, 10.2 million Class B ordinary shares and 158.1 million Class C
ordinary shares. These outstanding amounts do not include any ordinary shares issuable upon exercise or conversion of options or other convertible securities, including as a result of the conversion of Virgin Media&#146;s outstanding 6.50%
convertible senior notes due 2016. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The issuance of ordinary shares of the Company in connection with the Mergers, as
described above, was registered under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, pursuant to a registration statement on Form S&#150;4 (File No.&nbsp;333&#150;187100), filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (&#147;<U>SEC</U>&#148;) and
declared effective on May&nbsp;1, 2013 (the &#147;<U>Form S-4</U>&#148;). </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Pursuant to Rule 12g-3(c) under the Securities
Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the &#147;<U>Exchange Act</U>&#148;), the ordinary shares of the Company are deemed to be registered under Section&nbsp;12(b) of the Exchange Act and, accordingly, the Company (as the successor issuer to Liberty
Global) will be subject to the reporting obligations under Sections 13 and 15(d) of the Exchange Act. The three classes of ordinary shares of the Company will begin trading on June 10, 2013 on the NASDAQ Global Select Market under the same ticker
symbols &#147;LBTYA&#148;, &#147;LBTYB&#148; and &#147;LBTYK&#148;. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Based upon the facts available to the Company and its
current projections as of the date of this Current Report, the Company believes that, as structured, the exchange of Liberty Global common stock for ordinary shares of the Company pursuant to the Mergers may not be taxable to United States
(&#147;<U>U.S.</U>&#148;) stockholders of Liberty Global common stock for U.S. federal income tax purposes.&nbsp;However, the tax free treatment for the exchange of Liberty Global common stock for Company ordinary shares is not certain and depends
on various factual and legal inquiries. The factual determination regarding the tax treatment of the Mergers depends, in part, on the calculation of aggregate U.S. shareholder gain and tax </FONT></P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">2 </FONT></P>
